text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-A committee assigned to find out what happened to the wealth of Norwegian Jews deported to Nazi death camps during the war is deeply divided on how much additional compensation should be given to survivors. The committee is to submit its findings to the Justice Ministry on Monday.

-The Norwegian intelligence service will resume an investigation into so-called Lebensborn agents in Norway following revelations in German magazine Der Spiegel. Communist East Germany let its spies take over the identities of children born under Hitler's Lebensborn programme to infiltrate Norway and other Western countries, Der Spiegel said.
-The aviation authority plans to introduce lower landing fees for commercial flights, making it cheaper for airlines to start new routes in Norway.
-The Norwegian crown weakened sharply yesterday after foreign speculators sold crowns massively.
-Shares in Norsk Hydro fell to help drag down the Total index on the Oslo Bourse yesterday.
-Forestry group Norske Skog ASA is in talks with KS Hedalm Trelast on possibly merging their units for saw mills and board production into a new company after dropping similar talks with Moelven.
-Foreign investors are selling Norwegian crowns for German marks, weakening the crown considerably.
